spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m0p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Handlers, Cleared, Supervisor, NoReading, MaxRetry, MaxEdits

ASSUME Cleared \subseteq Handlers
ASSUME Supervisor \notin Handlers

Submitters == Handlers \cup {Supervisor}

VARIABLES editLog, reading, recall, retries

vars == <<editLog, reading, recall, retries>>

\* The version stamp of the routing record is just how many edits have landed.
Stamp == Len(editLog)

Entry == [by: Submitters, saw: 0..MaxEdits]

TypeOK ==
    /\ editLog \in Seq(Entry)
    /\ reading \in [Handlers -> (0..MaxEdits) \cup {NoReading}]
    /\ recall \in BOOLEAN
    /\ retries \in [Handlers -> 0..MaxRetry]

Init ==
    /\ editLog = << >>
    /\ reading = [h \in Handlers |-> NoReading]
    /\ recall = FALSE
    /\ retries = [h \in Handlers |-> 0]

\* A handler with no reading in hand takes one; uncleared staff may read too.
TakeReading(h) ==
    /\ reading[h] = NoReading
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![h] = Stamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<editLog, recall, retries>>

\* Accepted only when the reading is still current, the submitter is cleared,
\* and the record is not in recall mode.
Submit(h) ==
    /\ ~recall
    /\ h \in Cleared
    /\ reading[h] = Stamp
    /\ editLog' = Append(editLog, [by |-> h, saw |-> reading[h]])
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![h] = NoReading]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<recall, retries>>

\* A reading that has gone stale is thrown away and the work is redone.
Retry(h) ==
    /\ reading[h] # NoReading
    /\ reading[h] # Stamp
    /\ retries[h] < MaxRetry
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![h] = NoReading]
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![h] = retries[h] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<editLog, recall>>

\* The privileged override: the supervisor may push during recall mode.
Override ==
    /\ recall
    /\ editLog' = Append(editLog, [by |-> Supervisor, saw |-> Stamp])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, recall, retries>>

EnterRecall ==
    /\ ~recall
    /\ recall' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<editLog, reading, retries>>

LeaveRecall ==
    /\ recall
    /\ recall' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<editLog, reading, retries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : TakeReading(h) \/ Submit(h) \/ Retry(h)
    \/ Override \/ EnterRecall \/ LeaveRecall

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Bounded == Len(editLog) <= MaxEdits

\* Nothing lands unless it is both authorised and computed from the newest stamp.
NoStaleOrUnclearedEdit ==
    \A i \in DOMAIN editLog :
        /\ editLog[i].by \in Cleared \cup {Supervisor}
        /\ editLog[i].saw = i - 1

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Handlers = {hgate, hbelt, hramp}
    Cleared = {hgate, hbelt}
    Supervisor = supv
    NoReading = noread
    MaxRetry = 1
    MaxEdits = 3

CONSTRAINT Bounded

INVARIANT NoStaleOrUnclearedEdit
nl:
An airport baggage router keeps a single routing record that says which chute each flight's bags
go down. Ground handlers edit that record without taking it out of service: a handler first reads
the record and remembers the version stamp it saw, then later submits its recomputed routing. The
submission is accepted only if the version stamp it read is still the current one, so a handler
whose reading has gone stale must throw its work away and start over. Only handlers on the day's
security clearance list may submit at all; uncleared staff may read and recompute but their
submissions are never accepted.

During a diversion the record is put into recall mode. While recall mode is on, ordinary handler
submissions are refused outright, but the duty supervisor holds a privileged override and may push
a routing directly onto the record even though recall mode is on. Every accepted submission is
appended to the record's edit log together with the identity of whoever submitted it and the
version stamp that submission was computed from.

The full set of actions is: a handler takes a reading of the current version stamp; a cleared
handler submits a recomputed routing while recall mode is off and its reading is still current; a
handler whose reading has gone stale discards it and retries, up to a bounded number of retries;
the duty supervisor pushes a routing under the privileged override while recall mode is on; the
router enters recall mode; and the router leaves recall mode.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry in the edit log was submitted either by the duty supervisor or by a
handler on the clearance list, and was computed from exactly the version stamp that immediately
preceded it, so no stale or uncleared submission ever lands on the routing record.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m2p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cabins, MaxGeneration

VARIABLES phase, answer, stamp, generation, authorised

vars == <<phase, answer, stamp, generation, authorised>>

Phases == {"idle", "polling", "granted", "aborted"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in Phases
    /\ answer \in [Cabins -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ stamp \in [Cabins -> 0..MaxGeneration]
    /\ generation \in 0..MaxGeneration
    /\ authorised \subseteq Cabins

Unanimous == \A c \in Cabins : answer[c] = "yes"

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ answer = [c \in Cabins |-> "none"]
    /\ stamp = [c \in Cabins |-> 0]
    /\ generation = 0
    /\ authorised = Cabins

OpenPoll ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "polling"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<answer, stamp, generation, authorised>>

\* Only an authorised cabin may put an answer on the board, and the answer
\* carries the generation that was in force when it was given.
Record(c, v) ==
    /\ phase = "polling"
    /\ c \in authorised
    /\ answer[c] = "none"
    /\ answer' = [answer EXCEPT ![c] = v]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![c] = generation]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, generation, authorised>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "polling"
    /\ Unanimous
    /\ phase' = "granted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<answer, stamp, generation, authorised>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "polling"
    /\ ~Unanimous
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<answer, stamp, generation, authorised>>

Clear ==
    /\ phase \in {"granted", "aborted"}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ answer' = [c \in Cabins |-> "none"]
    /\ stamp' = [c \in Cabins |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<generation, authorised>>

\* Track work: everything decided under the old geometry is wiped.
Regenerate ==
    /\ generation < MaxGeneration
    /\ generation' = generation + 1
    /\ answer' = [c \in Cabins |-> "none"]
    /\ stamp' = [c \in Cabins |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, authorised>>

\* Suspension takes the cabin's standing answer down with it.
Suspend(c) ==
    /\ c \in authorised
    /\ authorised' = authorised \ {c}
    /\ answer' = [answer EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, generation>>

\* The control centre's privileged override skips the tally entirely.
Override ==
    /\ phase = "polling"
    /\ phase' = "granted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<answer, stamp, generation, authorised>>

Next ==
    \/ OpenPoll \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ Clear \/ Regenerate \/ Override
    \/ \E c \in Cabins : Record(c, "yes") \/ Record(c, "no") \/ Suspend(c)

RecordSome == \E c \in Cabins : Record(c, "yes")

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ SF_vars(Commit)
    /\ SF_vars(Abort)
    /\ WF_vars(RecordSome)

\* Nothing stale or unauthorised is left contributing to the tally.
StandingAnswersAreCurrent ==
    \A c \in Cabins :
        answer[c] # "none" => (c \in authorised /\ stamp[c] = generation)

\* Every poll that opens is eventually decided one way or the other.
PollAlwaysDecides == (phase = "polling") ~> (phase \in {"granted", "aborted"})

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Cabins = {cnorth, csouth}
    MaxGeneration = 2

INVARIANT StandingAnswersAreCurrent

PROPERTY PollAlwaysDecides
nl:
A subway signalling system hands out movement authority for a track block only after the
interlocking cabins that own the adjoining points all agree. A round begins when the control centre
opens a poll on the pending authority; each cabin then records a yes or a no, and its recorded
answer is stamped with the interlocking generation that was in force when it answered. The poll is
tallied only from answers that are still standing.

Two things can invalidate answers that are already on the board. The interlocking can be
regenerated after track work, which advances the generation number and wipes every standing answer
so that nothing decided under the old geometry is counted. Separately, the control centre can
suspend a cabin's authorisation, for example when its cabin loses its safety interlock; a suspended
cabin's standing answer is wiped at the same moment, and a suspended cabin may not answer again.
The control centre also holds a privileged override and can declare the authority granted without
waiting on the tally at all.

The full set of actions is: the control centre opens a poll; an authorised cabin records a yes; an
authorised cabin records a no; the poll commits when every cabin's standing answer is a yes; the
poll aborts when the standing answers are not all yes; the round is cleared back to idle after a
decision; the interlocking is regenerated, advancing the generation and wiping all standing
answers; the control centre suspends a cabin, wiping that cabin's standing answer; and the control
centre invokes its privileged override to grant the authority directly.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any answer still standing on the tally board belongs to a cabin whose
authorisation has not been suspended and carries the interlocking generation that is currently in
force, so a suspended or out-of-generation cabin never contributes to a movement authority.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every poll that is opened eventually reaches a decision, either committing the
movement authority or aborting the round.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m6p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Engines, Orders, MaxDepth, LeaseTicks

VARIABLES staged, unstaged, ticksLeft, depth

vars == <<staged, unstaged, ticksLeft, depth>>

\* Everything currently sitting in the crossing buffer, whoever put it there.
Buffered == UNION {staged[e] : e \in Engines}

Load == Cardinality(Buffered)

TypeOK ==
    /\ staged \in [Engines -> SUBSET Orders]
    /\ unstaged \subseteq Orders
    /\ ticksLeft \in [Engines -> 0..LeaseTicks]
    /\ depth \in 0..MaxDepth

Init ==
    /\ staged = [e \in Engines |-> {}]
    /\ unstaged = Orders
    /\ ticksLeft = [e \in Engines |-> 0]
    /\ depth = 1

\* An allocation is taken out for its full run of pre-open ticks.
TakeAllocation(e) ==
    /\ ticksLeft[e] = 0
    /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![e] = LeaseTicks]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, unstaged, depth>>

CountDown(e) ==
    /\ ticksLeft[e] > 0
    /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![e] = ticksLeft[e] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, unstaged, depth>>

\* Staging is refused unless the buffer is below the advertised depth.
Stage(e, o) ==
    /\ ticksLeft[e] > 0
    /\ o \in unstaged
    /\ Load < depth
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![e] = @ \cup {o}]
    /\ unstaged' = unstaged \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticksLeft, depth>>

\* A crossed order leaves the buffer permanently.
Cross(e, o) ==
    /\ o \in staged[e]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![e] = @ \ {o}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unstaged, ticksLeft, depth>>

\* Nothing survives the end of an allocation.
GiveBack(e) ==
    /\ ticksLeft[e] = 0
    /\ staged[e] # {}
    /\ unstaged' = unstaged \cup staged[e]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![e] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticksLeft, depth>>

Advertise ==
    /\ depth < MaxDepth
    /\ depth' = depth + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, unstaged, ticksLeft>>

\* Headroom is only withdrawn while there is headroom to withdraw.
Withdraw ==
    /\ depth > 0
    /\ Load < depth
    /\ depth' = depth - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, unstaged, ticksLeft>>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Engines :
         \/ TakeAllocation(e) \/ CountDown(e) \/ GiveBack(e)
         \/ \E o \in Orders : Stage(e, o) \/ Cross(e, o)
    \/ Advertise \/ Withdraw

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The buffer never holds more than the exchange says it can.
BufferWithinAdvertisedDepth == Load <= depth

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Engines = {eblue, egreen}
    Orders = {oa, ob, oc}
    MaxDepth = 3
    LeaseTicks = 2

INVARIANT BufferWithinAdvertisedDepth
nl:
Before a stock exchange opens, incoming orders are staged in a crossing buffer until the opening
auction runs. The buffer has an advertised depth, and the exchange republishes that depth during
the pre-open window as it sees how heavy the morning is: it can add headroom, and it can take
headroom away, but it will only shrink the advertised depth down as far as the number of orders
already staged, never below.

Staging is done by matching engines, and an engine may only stage orders while it holds a live
time-limited allocation on the buffer. An allocation is taken out for a fixed number of pre-open
ticks and counts down; when it reaches zero the engine has no allocation any more and can neither
stage new orders nor keep the ones it staged, so those orders are returned to the unstaged pool and
must be staged again by an engine that does hold one. An engine stages an order only when the
buffer still has room against the currently advertised depth. When the auction crosses an order it
leaves the buffer for good.

The full set of actions is: an engine without an allocation takes one out for the full number of
ticks; an engine's allocation counts down by one tick; an engine holding a live allocation stages
an unstaged order, provided the buffer is below the advertised depth; the auction crosses a staged
order, which leaves the buffer; an engine whose allocation has run out gives back everything it
staged to the unstaged pool; the exchange advertises one more unit of depth; and the exchange
withdraws one unit of depth, which it may do only while the staged count is strictly below the
depth it is withdrawing from.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of orders staged in the crossing buffer, counted across all matching
engines together, never exceeds the depth the exchange currently advertises.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m2p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Stations, Retags, NoRetag

ASSUME NoRetag \notin Retags

VARIABLES manifest, acked, phase, declared, active

vars == <<manifest, acked, phase, declared, active>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ manifest \subseteq Retags
    /\ acked \subseteq Retags
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "agreeing", "written"}
    /\ declared \in [Stations -> {"none", "ready", "refuse"}]
    /\ active \in Retags \cup {NoRetag}

AllReady == \A s \in Stations : declared[s] = "ready"

Init ==
    /\ manifest = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ declared = [s \in Stations |-> "none"]
    /\ active = NoRetag

\* The router is always free to open a fresh round on some re-tag.
OpenRound(r) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ active' = r
    /\ phase' = "agreeing"
    /\ declared' = [s \in Stations |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, acked>>

Declare(s, v) ==
    /\ phase = "agreeing"
    /\ declared[s] = "none"
    /\ declared' = [declared EXCEPT ![s] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, acked, phase, active>>

Write ==
    /\ phase = "agreeing"
    /\ AllReady
    /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {active}
    /\ phase' = "written"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, declared, active>>

\* The supervisor's privileged override skips the declarations entirely.
Override ==
    /\ phase = "agreeing"
    /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {active}
    /\ phase' = "written"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, declared, active>>

\* Telling the airline is the point of no return.
Acknowledge ==
    /\ phase = "written"
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {active}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ active' = NoRetag
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, declared>>

\* Backing out is available only before the acknowledgement has gone out.
BackOut ==
    /\ phase = "written"
    /\ active \notin acked
    /\ manifest' = manifest \ {active}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ active' = NoRetag
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, declared>>

Abandon ==
    /\ phase = "agreeing"
    /\ \E s \in Stations : declared[s] = "refuse"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ active' = NoRetag
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, acked, declared>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Retags : OpenRound(r)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Declare(s, "ready") \/ Declare(s, "refuse")
    \/ Write \/ Override \/ Acknowledge \/ BackOut \/ Abandon

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Acknowledge)

\* Anything the airline was promised is still on the manifest.
NoAcknowledgedRetagLost == acked \subseteq manifest

\* A landed write is never parked in the written state forever.
WrittenRoundsSettle == (phase = "written") ~> (phase = "idle")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Stations = {sintake, ssort}
    Retags = {rt1, rt2}
    NoRetag = rtnone

INVARIANT NoAcknowledgedRetagLost

PROPERTY WrittenRoundsSettle
nl:
An airport baggage router keeps a shared manifest listing which bags have been re-tagged for a
later flight. A re-tag is not written straight into the manifest: the router first runs an agreement
round with the sorter stations that touch the bag, and each station either declares itself ready or
refuses. When every station has declared ready, the re-tag is written into the manifest, and the
round is then in the written state. From there the router sends the airline its acknowledgement,
which is the point at which the airline is entitled to treat the re-tag as durable.

A write that has not yet been acknowledged may still be backed out: the router removes it from the
manifest and returns to idle, which is what happens when the round is torn down after the write but
before the airline is told. Once the acknowledgement has gone out, backing the write out is not
available. If any station refuses during the agreement round, the round is abandoned without a
write at all. The duty supervisor holds a privileged override and may push the round straight into
the written state without waiting for the stations to declare, which is used when a flight is
closing and the stations are too slow to poll.

The full set of actions is: the router opens an agreement round on some re-tag; a station
declares itself ready; a station refuses; the write lands in the manifest once every station has
declared ready; the acknowledgement goes out to the airline and the round returns to idle; the
round is abandoned when a station has refused; an unacknowledged write is backed out of the
manifest; and the duty supervisor overrides the round straight into the written state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every re-tag the airline has been sent an acknowledgement for is still present in
the shared manifest, so no acknowledged update is ever lost.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A round that has reached the written state never stays there indefinitely; it
eventually returns to idle.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m0p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, Bins, Scripts, Empty, NoBin, NoScript

ASSUME Empty \notin Scripts
ASSUME NoBin \notin Bins
ASSUME NoScript \notin Scripts

VARIABLES label, ticket, carrying, noted, stopped

vars == <<label, ticket, carrying, noted, stopped>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ label \in [Bins -> Scripts \cup {Empty}]
    /\ ticket \in [Scripts -> Bins \cup {NoBin}]
    /\ carrying \in [Robots -> Scripts \cup {NoScript}]
    /\ noted \in [Robots -> Bins \cup {NoBin}]
    /\ stopped \subseteq Robots

Working(r) == r \notin stopped

Init ==
    /\ label = [b \in Bins |-> Empty]
    /\ ticket = [s \in Scripts |-> NoBin]
    /\ carrying = [r \in Robots |-> NoScript]
    /\ noted = [r \in Robots |-> NoBin]
    /\ stopped = {}

PickUp(r, s) ==
    /\ Working(r)
    /\ carrying[r] = NoScript
    /\ ticket[s] = NoBin
    /\ \A q \in Robots : carrying[q] # s
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![r] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<label, ticket, noted, stopped>>

\* The optimistic read: a bin seen empty is noted, but nothing is reserved.
NoteBin(r, b) ==
    /\ Working(r)
    /\ carrying[r] # NoScript
    /\ noted[r] = NoBin
    /\ label[b] = Empty
    /\ noted' = [noted EXCEPT ![r] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<label, ticket, carrying, stopped>>

\* The drop re-checks the bin; a bin taken in the meantime is not written over.
Drop(r) ==
    /\ Working(r)
    /\ noted[r] # NoBin
    /\ carrying[r] # NoScript
    /\ label[noted[r]] = Empty
    /\ label' = [label EXCEPT ![noted[r]] = carrying[r]]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![carrying[r]] = noted[r]]
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![r] = NoScript]
    /\ noted' = [noted EXCEPT ![r] = NoBin]
    /\ UNCHANGED stopped

GoLookAgain(r) ==
    /\ Working(r)
    /\ noted[r] # NoBin
    /\ label[noted[r]] # Empty
    /\ noted' = [noted EXCEPT ![r] = NoBin]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<label, ticket, carrying, stopped>>

\* A robot can stop dead with work still in its hands.
Stop(r) ==
    /\ Working(r)
    /\ stopped' = stopped \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<label, ticket, carrying, noted>>

\* A technician power-cycles a stopped robot; its half-done work is abandoned.
Restart(r) ==
    /\ ~Working(r)
    /\ stopped' = stopped \ {r}
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![r] = NoScript]
    /\ noted' = [noted EXCEPT ![r] = NoBin]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<label, ticket>>

Collect(b) ==
    /\ label[b] # Empty
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![label[b]] = NoBin]
    /\ label' = [label EXCEPT ![b] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carrying, noted, stopped>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots :
         \/ Drop(r) \/ GoLookAgain(r) \/ Stop(r) \/ Restart(r)
         \/ \E s \in Scripts : PickUp(r, s)
         \/ \E b \in Bins : NoteBin(r, b)
    \/ \E b \in Bins : Collect(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Ticket and label agree, which is what stops one bin serving two patients.
TicketsAgreeWithLabels ==
    \A s \in Scripts : ticket[s] # NoBin => label[ticket[s]] = s

====
nl:
A pharmacy's dispensing wall is a row of pickup bins. When a prescription is ready, a dispensing
robot puts the bagged prescription into a bin, writes the prescription's name on the bin's label,
and the patient is handed a ticket naming that bin. The robots do not reserve bins ahead of time.
A robot that is carrying a prescription looks along the wall for a bin it sees standing empty and
notes that bin down; later, when it actually goes to put the bag in, it looks at the bin again and
only completes the drop if the bin is still empty. If some other robot got there first, the noted
bin is discarded and the robot goes looking again.

A robot can stop dead at any moment without telling anyone. A robot that has stopped takes no
further part: it does not complete a drop, it does not go looking again, and whatever it was
carrying and whichever bin it had noted stay frozen with it. The rest of the wall keeps working
around it until a technician power-cycles it, at which point it comes back empty-handed with no bin
noted.

When a patient collects, the bag leaves the bin, the bin's label is wiped, and the ticket for that
prescription stops naming a bin.

The full set of actions is: a working robot picks up a prescription that has not yet been given a
ticket; a working robot carrying a prescription notes down a bin it currently sees empty; a working
robot completes the drop into its noted bin, provided the bin is still empty at that moment, which
writes the bin's label and issues the patient's ticket; a working robot discards a noted bin that
is no longer empty and goes looking again; a robot stops dead; a technician power-cycles a stopped
robot, which abandons whatever it was carrying and whichever bin it had noted; and a patient
collects from a labelled bin, wiping the label and the ticket.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a patient's ticket names a bin, that bin's label names that same
prescription, so the wall never hands two patients tickets to one bin.

---- MODULE W4Od9m3p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Feeders, Slots, Demand, MaxBlock, Home, NoLeader, Free

ASSUME Home \in Feeders
ASSUME NoLeader \notin Feeders

Order == [dest : Feeders, block : 1..MaxBlock]

VARIABLES energised, pool, bus, coordinator

vars == <<energised, pool, bus, coordinator>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ energised \in [Feeders -> 0..Demand]
    /\ pool \in 0..Demand
    /\ bus \in [Slots -> Order \cup {Free}]
    /\ coordinator \in Feeders \cup {NoLeader}

RECURSIVE OnFeeders(_)
OnFeeders(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET f == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN energised[f] + OnFeeders(S \ {f})

RECURSIVE OnBus(_)
OnBus(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN
         (IF bus[s] = Free THEN 0 ELSE bus[s].block) + OnBus(S \ {s})

Init ==
    /\ energised = [f \in Feeders |-> IF f = Home THEN Demand ELSE 0]
    /\ pool = 0
    /\ bus = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ coordinator = NoLeader

TakeOver(f) ==
    /\ coordinator = NoLeader
    /\ coordinator' = f
    /\ UNCHANGED <<energised, pool, bus>>

DropOut ==
    /\ coordinator # NoLeader
    /\ coordinator' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<energised, pool, bus>>

\* Shedding moves a block off a feeder and parks it; nothing is destroyed.
Shed(f, k) ==
    /\ coordinator # NoLeader
    /\ energised[f] >= k
    /\ energised' = [energised EXCEPT ![f] = @ - k]
    /\ pool' = pool + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, coordinator>>

\* Issuing debits the source immediately; the block now rides on the bus.
Issue(f, k, s) ==
    /\ coordinator # NoLeader
    /\ pool >= k
    /\ bus[s] = Free
    /\ pool' = pool - k
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![s] = [dest |-> f, block |-> k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<energised, coordinator>>

\* Any outstanding order may be applied; the bus does not preserve order.
Apply(s) ==
    /\ bus[s] # Free
    /\ energised' = [energised EXCEPT ![bus[s].dest] = @ + bus[s].block]
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, coordinator>>

Move(f, g, k, s) ==
    /\ coordinator # NoLeader
    /\ f # g
    /\ energised[f] >= k
    /\ bus[s] = Free
    /\ energised' = [energised EXCEPT ![f] = @ - k]
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![s] = [dest |-> g, block |-> k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, coordinator>>

TakeOverSome == \E f \in Feeders : TakeOver(f)

Next ==
    \/ TakeOverSome \/ DropOut
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Apply(s)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, k \in 1..MaxBlock : Shed(f, k)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders, k \in 1..MaxBlock, s \in Slots : Issue(f, k, s)
    \/ \E f, g \in Feeders : \E k \in 1..MaxBlock, s \in Slots : Move(f, g, k, s)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(TakeOverSome)

\* Every megawatt is somewhere: on a feeder, in the pool, or on the bus.
DemandConserved == OnFeeders(Feeders) + pool + OnBus(Slots) = Demand

\* The region never sits leaderless for good.
CoordinatorRestored == (coordinator = NoLeader) ~> (coordinator # NoLeader)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Feeders = {fnorth, fsouth}
    Slots = {bus1, bus2}
    Demand = 3
    MaxBlock = 2
    Home = fnorth
    NoLeader = nocoord
    Free = slotfree

INVARIANT DemandConserved

PROPERTY CoordinatorRestored
nl:
A regional power grid runs a load shedder. The region carries a fixed number of megawatts of
customer demand, and every megawatt is at all times in exactly one of three places: energised on
one of the feeders, parked in the shed pool waiting to be brought back, or riding on a dispatch
order that has left the control room but has not yet been applied at the receiving feeder.

Dispatch orders travel over the grid's telemetry bus, which does not preserve order: several orders
can be outstanding at once and they may be applied in any sequence, not necessarily the sequence
they were issued in. An order names one receiving feeder and a block of megawatts. The block is
taken off its source the moment the order is issued and only appears on the receiving feeder when
the order is applied, so it is never counted in two places and never disappears in between.

Shedding and dispatching are directed by the control room's coordinator, which is one of the
feeders acting in that role. The coordinator can drop out at any moment, leaving the region with no
coordinator; any feeder can then take the role over. While there is no coordinator, no load is shed
and no dispatch order is issued, though orders already on the bus can still be applied.

The full set of actions is: a feeder takes over as coordinator when there is none; the sitting
coordinator drops out; under a coordinator, a block is shed off a feeder into the shed pool; under
a coordinator, a block is taken out of the shed pool and issued as a dispatch order onto a free
slot on the bus; an outstanding order is applied, adding its block to the receiving feeder and
freeing its slot; and a block is moved directly off one feeder onto the bus as an order addressed
to another feeder.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The megawatts energised across all feeders, plus those parked in the shed pool,
plus those riding on outstanding dispatch orders, always add up to exactly the region's fixed
demand.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the region is left without a coordinator, some feeder eventually takes
the role over.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Lines, Blowers, EntryDepth, NoRead

VARIABLES counter, remembered, drying, queued

vars == <<counter, remembered, drying, queued>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ counter \in 0..Blowers
    /\ remembered \in [Lines -> (0..Blowers) \cup {NoRead}]
    /\ drying \in [Lines -> 0..Blowers]
    /\ queued \in [Lines -> 0..EntryDepth]

RECURSIVE InTunnel(_)
InTunnel(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET l == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN drying[l] + InTunnel(S \ {l})

Init ==
    /\ counter = 0
    /\ remembered = [l \in Lines |-> NoRead]
    /\ drying = [l \in Lines |-> 0]
    /\ queued = [l \in Lines |-> 0]

Arrive(l) ==
    /\ queued[l] < EntryDepth
    /\ queued' = [queued EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, remembered, drying>>

\* The read half: the line notes the figure it saw and reserves nothing.
ReadCounter(l) ==
    /\ remembered[l] = NoRead
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![l] = counter]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, drying, queued>>

\* The write half: it takes effect only if the counter still matches.
Book(l) ==
    /\ remembered[l] # NoRead
    /\ remembered[l] = counter
    /\ remembered[l] < Blowers
    /\ queued[l] > 0
    /\ counter' = remembered[l] + 1
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![l] = NoRead]
    /\ drying' = [drying EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ queued' = [queued EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]

\* The other line got there first, so the remembered figure is worthless.
Reread(l) ==
    /\ remembered[l] # NoRead
    /\ remembered[l] # counter
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![l] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, drying, queued>>

Leave(l) ==
    /\ drying[l] > 0
    /\ counter > 0
    /\ drying' = [drying EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
    /\ counter' = counter - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remembered, queued>>

Next ==
    \E l \in Lines : Arrive(l) \/ ReadCounter(l) \/ Book(l) \/ Reread(l) \/ Leave(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The two lines together never put more cars under the blowers than there are.
TunnelWithinBlowerBank == InTunnel(Lines) <= Blowers

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Lines = {lwest, least}
    Blowers = 3
    EntryDepth = 2
    NoRead = noread

INVARIANT TunnelWithinBlowerBank
nl:
A car-wash site runs two conveyor lines side by side. The lines are otherwise independent, but they
share a single bank of hot-air blowers, and a car cannot enter the drying tunnel unless a blower is
free for it. The number of blowers is fixed and is the site's shared capacity.

Availability is tracked in one shared booking counter that both lines can see. There is no
reservation desk: a line that wants to send a car into the drying tunnel first reads the booking
counter and remembers the figure it read, and then, when it is ready to move the car, writes back
the figure it read plus one. That write only takes effect if the counter still holds exactly the
figure the line remembered; if the other line has booked in the meantime the counter no longer
matches, the remembered figure is thrown away, and the line reads again. A line will only attempt
the write if the figure it remembered was still below the site's capacity.

Cars queue at the entry of each line before they are booked in, and when a car comes out of the
drying tunnel the booking counter is decremented and the car leaves the site.

The full set of actions is: a car arrives and joins the entry queue of one of the lines; a line
reads the shared booking counter and remembers the figure; a line whose remembered figure is still
below capacity and still matches the counter writes back that figure plus one, which moves a queued
car into the drying tunnel; a line whose remembered figure no longer matches the counter throws it
away and will read again; and a car leaves the drying tunnel, which decrements the booking counter.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars inside the shared drying tunnel, counted across both conveyor
lines together, never exceeds the number of blowers the site has.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m8p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Terminals, Bays, Carts, StartBay, Unclaimed

ASSUME StartBay \in Bays

VARIABLES inBay, onApron, yardClaim, bayClaim

vars == <<inBay, onApron, yardClaim, bayClaim>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ inBay \in [Bays -> 0..Carts]
    /\ onApron \in [Terminals -> 0..Carts]
    /\ yardClaim \in Terminals \cup {Unclaimed}
    /\ bayClaim \in [Bays -> Terminals \cup {Unclaimed}]

RECURSIVE Standing(_)
Standing(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN inBay[b] + Standing(S \ {b})

RECURSIVE OutWith(_)
OutWith(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET t == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN onApron[t] + OutWith(S \ {t})

Init ==
    /\ inBay = [b \in Bays |-> IF b = StartBay THEN Carts ELSE 0]
    /\ onApron = [t \in Terminals |-> 0]
    /\ yardClaim = Unclaimed
    /\ bayClaim = [b \in Bays |-> Unclaimed]

TakeYard(t) ==
    /\ yardClaim = Unclaimed
    /\ yardClaim' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, onApron, bayClaim>>

\* Coarse before fine: no bay claim without the yard-wide claim.
TakeBay(t, b) ==
    /\ yardClaim = t
    /\ bayClaim[b] = Unclaimed
    /\ bayClaim' = [bayClaim EXCEPT ![b] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, onApron, yardClaim>>

\* A cart leaves the bay and appears on the apron in the same step.
Draw(t, b) ==
    /\ bayClaim[b] = t
    /\ inBay[b] > 0
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
    /\ onApron' = [onApron EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yardClaim, bayClaim>>

DropBay(t, b) ==
    /\ bayClaim[b] = t
    /\ bayClaim' = [bayClaim EXCEPT ![b] = Unclaimed]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, onApron, yardClaim>>

\* Giving up the yard drops everything the terminal was holding under it.
DropYard(t) ==
    /\ yardClaim = t
    /\ yardClaim' = Unclaimed
    /\ bayClaim' = [b \in Bays |-> IF bayClaim[b] = t THEN Unclaimed ELSE bayClaim[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, onApron>>

Return(t, b) ==
    /\ onApron[t] > 0
    /\ onApron' = [onApron EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
    /\ inBay' = [inBay EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yardClaim, bayClaim>>

DropYardSome == \E t \in Terminals : DropYard(t)

Next ==
    \/ DropYardSome
    \/ \E t \in Terminals :
         \/ TakeYard(t)
         \/ \E b \in Bays : TakeBay(t, b) \/ Draw(t, b) \/ DropBay(t, b) \/ Return(t, b)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(DropYardSome)

\* Every cart is either standing in a bay or out with a terminal.
CartsConserved == Standing(Bays) + OutWith(Terminals) = Carts

\* Nobody keeps the shared yard to themselves for ever.
YardEventuallyFreed == (yardClaim # Unclaimed) ~> (yardClaim = Unclaimed)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Terminals = {tnorth, tsouth}
    Bays = {baya, bayb}
    Carts = 3
    StartBay = baya
    Unclaimed = unclaimed

INVARIANT CartsConserved

PROPERTY YardEventuallyFreed
nl:
An airport runs two baggage routers, one per terminal, and they are operationally independent except
that they draw tote carts from a single shared cart yard. The yard is split into bays. Every tote
cart on the airfield is at every moment in exactly one place: standing in one of the yard's bays,
or out on the apron with one of the two terminals. Carts are never built and never scrapped during
a shift, so the airfield's cart count is fixed.

Drawing from the yard is done in two steps, coarse before fine. A terminal that wants carts first
takes the yard-wide claim, which only one terminal can hold at a time. Holding the yard-wide claim,
it may then take a bay claim on one or more individual bays; a bay claim can only be taken by the
terminal that currently holds the yard-wide claim, and only if no one else already has that bay. It
draws a cart out of a bay it has claimed, and the cart goes out with that terminal.

A terminal can give back an individual bay claim on its own. It can also give up the yard-wide
claim outright, and doing so drops every bay claim it was holding at the same time, so the yard is
left completely free for the other terminal. Returning carts needs no claim at all: a terminal can
push a cart it holds back into any bay at any time.

The full set of actions is: a terminal takes the yard-wide claim when no one holds it; the holder of
the yard-wide claim takes a claim on a free bay; a terminal draws one cart out of a bay it has
claimed, provided that bay is not empty; a terminal gives back one of its bay claims; a terminal
gives up the yard-wide claim, which also drops all the bay claims it was holding; and a terminal
pushes one of its carts back into a bay.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The carts standing in the yard's bays plus the carts out with the two terminals
always add up to exactly the airfield's fixed cart count.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The yard-wide claim is never held forever; whenever a terminal takes it, the
yard eventually becomes unclaimed again.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m7p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Free, MoveBudget

ASSUME Free \notin Cranes

VARIABLES register, inLane, attempting, movesLeft

vars == <<register, inLane, attempting, movesLeft>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ register \in Cranes \cup {Free}
    /\ inLane \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ attempting \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ movesLeft \in [Cranes -> 0..MoveBudget]

Init ==
    /\ register = Free
    /\ inLane = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
    /\ attempting = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
    /\ movesLeft = [c \in Cranes |-> MoveBudget]

\* The read half of the swap: seeing "free" is not the same as holding it.
Look(c) ==
    /\ ~attempting[c]
    /\ ~inLane[c]
    /\ register = Free
    /\ attempting' = [attempting EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, inLane, movesLeft>>

\* The write half: it only lands while the register still reads "free".
Swap(c) ==
    /\ attempting[c]
    /\ register = Free
    /\ register' = c
    /\ attempting' = [attempting EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inLane, movesLeft>>

Abandon(c) ==
    /\ attempting[c]
    /\ register # Free
    /\ attempting' = [attempting EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, inLane, movesLeft>>

MoveIn(c) ==
    /\ register = c
    /\ ~inLane[c]
    /\ inLane' = [inLane EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, attempting, movesLeft>>

Lift(c) ==
    /\ inLane[c]
    /\ movesLeft[c] > 0
    /\ movesLeft' = [movesLeft EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, inLane, attempting>>

PullOut(c) ==
    /\ inLane[c]
    /\ inLane' = [inLane EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ register' = Free
    /\ movesLeft' = [movesLeft EXCEPT ![c] = MoveBudget]
    /\ UNCHANGED attempting

\* The supervisor's override hands the lane over and clears it in one step.
Override(c) ==
    /\ register' = c
    /\ inLane' = [d \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempting, movesLeft>>

Next ==
    \E c \in Cranes :
        Look(c) \/ Swap(c) \/ Abandon(c) \/ MoveIn(c) \/ Lift(c) \/ PullOut(c) \/ Override(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Whoever is in the lane is the crane the register names; nobody else can be.
LaneMatchesRegister == \A c \in Cranes : inLane[c] => register = c

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {gq1, gq2, gq3}
    Free = lanefree
    MoveBudget = 2

INVARIANT LaneMatchesRegister
nl:
A container-ship crane yard has several gantry cranes that all need the same single transfer lane
running under the ship's side. Only one crane may be standing in that lane at a time, because two
booms over the same lane will foul each other.

The lane is guarded by one register that either reads "free" or carries the name of a crane. A
crane that wants the lane first looks at the register; if what it saw was "free" it then attempts
the swap, writing its own name in place of "free". The swap only goes through while the register
still reads "free", so if another crane wrote its name first, the attempt is abandoned and the
crane will look again later. A crane whose name is in the register may then move into the lane, do
a bounded number of container moves, and finally pull out, which puts the register back to "free".

The yard supervisor holds a privileged override for emergencies such as a shifted load. Invoking
the override writes a chosen crane's name into the register directly, without any swap, and at the
same instant pulls every crane out of the lane, so the chosen crane starts from a clear lane.

The full set of actions is: a crane that is neither attempting nor in the lane looks at the
register; a crane that saw "free" completes the swap, writing its own name, provided the register
still reads "free"; a crane abandons its attempt because the register no longer reads "free"; the
crane whose name is in the register moves into the lane; a crane in the lane performs one container
move; a crane pulls out of the lane and sets the register back to "free"; and the supervisor
invokes the override, writing a chosen crane's name into the register and clearing the lane of
every crane.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any crane standing in the transfer lane is the crane whose name the register
currently carries, so two cranes are never in the lane together.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m2p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Drones, Controllers, Sectors, Ceiling, Ground, NoRound

ASSUME Ground \notin Sectors

VARIABLES station, phase, answer, silent, round

vars == <<station, phase, answer, silent, round>>

Rounds == [drone : Drones, sector : Sectors]

TypeOK ==
    /\ station \in [Drones -> Sectors \cup {Ground}]
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ answer \in [Controllers -> {"none", "clear", "object"}]
    /\ silent \subseteq Controllers
    /\ round \in Rounds \cup {NoRound}

Occupancy(s) == Cardinality({d \in Drones : station[d] = s})

Responding == Controllers \ silent

Init ==
    /\ station = [d \in Drones |-> Ground]
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ answer = [c \in Controllers |-> "none"]
    /\ silent = {}
    /\ round = NoRound

Open(d, s) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ station[d] = Ground
    /\ round' = [drone |-> d, sector |-> s]
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ answer' = [c \in Controllers |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<station, silent>>

Answer(c, v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ c \notin silent
    /\ answer[c] = "none"
    /\ answer' = [answer EXCEPT ![c] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<station, phase, silent, round>>

\* A controller can drop off the air mid-round without announcing it.
GoSilent(c) ==
    /\ c \notin silent
    /\ silent' = silent \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<station, phase, answer, round>>

ComeBack(c) ==
    /\ c \in silent
    /\ silent' = silent \ {c}
    /\ answer' = [answer EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<station, phase, round>>

\* The ceiling is re-checked at the moment of commit, not at proposal time.
Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A c \in Responding : answer[c] = "clear"
    /\ Occupancy(round.sector) < Ceiling
    /\ station' = [station EXCEPT ![round.drone] = round.sector]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ round' = NoRound
    /\ UNCHANGED <<answer, silent>>

Drop ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \/ \E c \in Responding : answer[c] = "object"
       \/ Occupancy(round.sector) >= Ceiling
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ round' = NoRound
    /\ UNCHANGED <<station, answer, silent>>

\* The all-aircraft recall brings everything home in one sweep.
Recall ==
    /\ \E d \in Drones : station[d] # Ground
    /\ station' = [d \in Drones |-> Ground]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, answer, silent, round>>

Next ==
    \/ Commit \/ Drop \/ Recall
    \/ \E d \in Drones, s \in Sectors : Open(d, s)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Answer(c, "clear") \/ Answer(c, "object")
                              \/ GoSilent(c) \/ ComeBack(c)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Recall)

\* No sector is ever holding more drones than its separation ceiling allows.
SectorCeilingRespected == \A s \in Sectors : Occupancy(s) <= Ceiling

\* Nothing stays up for ever; the recall always brings the swarm down.
EveryDroneLands == \A d \in Drones : (station[d] # Ground) ~> (station[d] = Ground)

====
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm flies drones over a fire, and the airspace over the fire is carved
into sectors. Each sector has a ceiling on how many drones may be inside it at once, set by the
separation the aircraft need from each other and from the water bombers.

A drone is never simply flown into a sector. The swarm controller opens an agreement round naming
one grounded drone and one sector, and each airspace controller then either clears the round or
objects to it. The round is committed only if every controller that is still responding has cleared
it and the named sector is currently below its ceiling; committing puts that drone into that
sector. The round is dropped if a responding controller objects, or if the named sector has
meanwhile filled up to its ceiling.

An airspace controller can go silent at any moment without saying so, and once silent it neither
clears nor objects to anything. A round is not held up by a silent controller: the decision is
taken over the controllers that are still responding. A silent controller can later come back on
the air, and it comes back with no answer recorded for the round in progress.

Finally, the swarm runs an all-aircraft recall: whenever any drone is still airborne, the recall can
be called, and every airborne drone lands and returns to the ground pool.

The full set of actions is: the swarm controller opens a round on a grounded drone and a sector; a
responding controller clears the round; a responding controller objects to the round; a controller
goes silent; a silent controller comes back on the air with its answer wiped; the round commits,
putting the drone into the sector, when every responding controller has cleared it and the sector
is below its ceiling; the round is dropped when a responding controller has objected or the sector
is at its ceiling; and the all-aircraft recall lands every airborne drone.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of drones inside any one sector never exceeds that sector's ceiling.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every drone that goes airborne eventually returns to the ground pool.
